A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same REFORM study, with 44 complete pages including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content; differences are confined to the title, running headers, and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on failure discovery, reward robustness, and downstream alignment using Anthropic HH and PKU Beavertails. Appendices B, D, and E contain additional experimental results and examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including reward-utility measurements in Tables 2–3, alignment results, and the supplementary analyses and examples.

M1.justification: The controlled-decoding objectives, selection of the lowest-loss 5% of training samples, failure filtering, and reward retraining are identical in Section 3 and Appendices B and G.

E1.justification: Both versions use Anthropic HH and PKU Beavertails with the same failure-discovery tasks, four perturbation scenarios, and BoN, PPO, and DPO alignment evaluations.

E2.justification: Figure 5 retains random perturbation and attribute-based prompting; Figure 6 retains Original Reward and RRM. The downstream alignment comparisons and Appendix B training comparators also match.

E3.justification: The 512-example test samples, model configurations, evaluation metrics, generation settings, and training protocols are unchanged in Section 4, figure captions, and the appendices.

E4.justification: The perturbation tests, top-k sensitivity observations, retraining-versus-finetuning comparison, attribute analyses, reward-distribution analysis, and qualitative examples are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical throughout both PDFs. No run-count or seed disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including the appendices. Table 2 retains Original/REFORM win rates of 63.28%/62.69% for HH and 68.75%/67.01% for PKU.

T1.justification: The failure-mode definition, decoding objectives and derivation, Appendix B regularization expression, and Appendix C metric formulas are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about tractable failure discovery, improved robustness, and preserved downstream utility. The revised title rephrases the existing self-improvement claim without changing its scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning spurious correlations and alignment quality are identical. The limitations on interpretability, exhaustive failure discovery, and universal robustness, together with the appendix qualifications, are unchanged.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, LoRA settings, evaluation templates in Appendix F, implementation listings in Appendix G, and the code-access link are identical.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to reward hacking, counterfactual generation, and controlled decoding.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Reward Models Can Improve Themselves: Reward-Guided Adversarial Failure Mode Discovery for Robust Reward Modeling' to 'Teach a Reward Model to Correct Itself: Reward Guided Adversarial Failure Discovery for Robust Reward Modeling'. Running headers and the arXiv version/date stamp are updated; body wording and organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–14 and Tables 1–12 retain identical content, captions, structure, and placement. The revised title occupies the same three-line block, and all page bodies retain identical layout.

improvement.justification: v3 only retitles the paper and updates its headers and version/date stamp. The methods, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility material—including all appendices—remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
